title: Vaccine-associated paralytic poliomyelitis: a case report of flaccid monoparesis after oral polio vaccine.
ehr_evidence: The report is based on clinical evaluation of a single patient at the Department of Pediatrics, Chonbuk National University Hospital, including physical/neurologic examination, laboratory tests, skeletal radiography, hip sonogram, 3-phase bone scan, brain and spinal MRI, and electrodiagnostic evaluations; no electronic health record or database was analysed.
summary: A single-case report describing a 4-month-old male who developed flaccid monoparesis of the left lower extremity four weeks after receiving oral polio vaccine (OPV) with DTaP and was left with permanent hypotonic monoparesis.
key_findings: The patient was left with permanent hypotonic monoparesis (GIV/V) with atrophy on the left lower extremity and ipsilateral claw foot persisting for more than 18 months despite massive physical therapy.
Attempts to isolate Sabin-like (vaccine-related) poliovirus in two stool and CSF samples failed because specimens were collected more than 2 months after onset of paralysis.
The patient is reported as the first clinically confirmed, officially approved recipient vaccine-associated paralytic poliomyelitis case in Korea.
captured_features: flaccid paralysis of the left lower extremity
muscle atrophy of the left lower extremity
electrodiagnostic findings (normal sensory nerve action potentials, low amplitudes in left tibial and deep peroneal nerves, widespread fibrillation potentials)
population: A single 4-month-old male patient (later followed to 2 years) treated at Chonbuk National University Hospital, Korea
exposure_domain: vaccine (oral polio vaccine, OPV, with DTaP)
limitations: Single case report with only one patient, limiting generalizability.
Failure to isolate the causative vaccine-related poliovirus from stool and CSF specimens, so etiology could not be virologically confirmed.
VAPP cannot be distinguished clinically from wild-type poliomyelitis.
